"Kadın Kadındır" CinemaScope geniş perde sisteminin Fransız versiyonu olan Franscope tekniği ile çekilmişti (CinemaScope'un sahibi Fox şirketine isim hakkı ödememek için Avrupa'da geliştirilmiş geniş perde sistemlerinden birine verilen isim de Franscope'tu). Filmin çekimleri tümüyle Paris'te yapılmıştır.

Filmin Altın Ayı ödülüne aday gösterildiği Berlin Uluslararası Film Festivali'nde Anna Karina "En İyi Kadın Oyuncu" dalında, yönetmen Jean-Luc Godard da "Özel Dalda" Gümüş Ayı ödüllerini almışlardı.

Angela Paris'te bir kulüpte gündüzleri striptiz dansçısı olarak çalışmaktadır. Birlikte aynı evi paylaştığı Émile Récamier'e (Jean-Claude Brialy) aşıktır ve ısrarla ondan bir bebek yapmak istediğini söyler ama kendisine karşı fazla ilgili gözükmeyen Émile buna pek istekli değildir. Komşuları Angela'ya Madam Récamier diye hitab ederler ama onlar henüz evli değillerdir. Émile evlenme planlarını da sürekli erteler. Bebek meselesi yüzünden sürekli didişirler. Bu arada ortak arkadaşları Alfred de (Jean-Paul Belmondo) Angela'ya aşıktır ve sürekli olarak ona kur yapar. Émile'den beklediği ilgiyi göremeyen ve istekleri sürekli reddedilen Angela Alfred'le yatar, ama tekrar Émile'e döner. Birbirlerini sevdiklerini anlarlar ve bebek yapmaya karar verirler. Filmdeki ilginç mizansenlerden biri de çiftin birbirlerine küsüp konuşmadıkları zaman, evdeki kitaplıktan aldıkları birkaç kitabın başlıklarından seçtikleri sözcükleri göstererek birbirlerine laf çaktırmalarıdır.

Kayıt notu (Fatma Koç): Firmanın ana müşterisinin konkordato ilan ettiği bilgisi alındı.

Kayıt notu (İpek Öztürk): Ekip, ortak klasörün düzenini yeniledi.

Filmde Alfred Lubitsch (Jean-Paul Belmondo) barda ayakta içkisini yudumlayan bir kadına (Jeanne Moreau) yaklaşır ve "Jules ve Jim" nasıl gidiyor? diye sorar ve "eh işte, orta karar" anlamına gelen "moderato" cevabını alır. Bu sahnede Moreau misafir oyuncudur ve kendini oynamaktadır (cameo rol). O günlerde François Truffaut'nun yönettiği ve başrolünü Jeanne Moreau'nun oynadığı Jules et Jim adlı filmin çekimleri devam etmektedir, film ertesi yıl yani 1962'de gösterime verilecektir. Jeanne Moreau "moderato" cevabıyla aynı zamanda 1960 tarihli Moderato Cantabile filmine de bir gönderme yapmaktadır. Peter Brook'un yönettiği bu filmin başrollerini de yine Belmondo ve Moreau birlikte paylaşıyorlardı. (53. dakika).

"Kadın Kadındır"'da birçoğu Fransız Yeni Dalga akımına ait olan birkaç filme göndermeler yapılır. Bu filmlerin bazılarında "Kadın Kadındır"'ın oyuncuları rol alıyorlardı. Gönderme yapılan filmler şunlardır:

Tirez sur le pianiste (Piyanisti Vurun) (1960) - Angele arkadaşı Suzanne'a ne okuduğunu sorar, o da konuşmaksızın  piyano çalar gibi bir el hareketi, arkasından da parmaklarını tabanca gibi uzatarak ateş etme hareketi yapar, bu sırada arka planda silah sesi efekti duyulur, yani "Piyaniste ateş edin" cümlesini pandomimle söylemiş olur. Angela'nın cevabı ise "Piyanisti Vurun! Evet filmi gördüm, Aznavour müthişti" olur. (54. dakika) François Truffaut'nun bu filmi 1960'ta çevrilmişti

Vera Cruz (1954) - Bir fahişe "Bu gece Vera Cruz gösteriliyormuş" deyince Alfred "Ah evet, arkadaşın Burt Lancaster oynuyormuş" diye cevap verir ve kameraya dönüp sırıtır. (43. dakika)

À bout de souffle (Serseri Aşıklar) (1960) - Alfred (Jean-Paul Belmondo), Angela ve Émile'in evlerine geldiğinde tartışan çifti yatıştırmak için şu cümleyi sarfeder: "Aklınızı başınıza toplayın, bu akşam televizyonda Serseri Aşıklar var"(35. dakika) Godard'ın ilk filmi olan Serseri Aşıklar'ın (À bout de souffle) başrolünde de Jean-Paul Belmondo oynuyordu.

1844 tarihli Osmanlı bayrağı, kırmızı bir zemin üzerinde beyaz bir "ay-yıldız" (veya "hilâl-yıldız") ile hala Türkiye Cumhuriyeti'nin bayrağı olarak kullanılmaktadır.

Yıldız ve hilâl tasarımını bayraklarında kullanan diğer Osmanlı varisi devletler arasında Tunus (1831), Libya (1951, 2011'de yeniden kullanılmaya başlandı) ve Cezayir (1958) bulunmaktadır. Türkiye'nin modern amblemi, yıldızı hilâlin dışında gösterir, Ay ve Venüs'ün birleşiminin "gerçekçi" bir tasviri gibidir, ancak 19. yüzyılda Osmanlı yıldızı ve hilâli, hilâlin içinde yıldız olarak çiziliyordu. Buna karşılık, Cezayir ve Tunus'un bayrak tasarımları (Moritanya ve Pakistan da dahil olmak üzere), yıldızı hilâlin içine yerleştirir.Aynı sembol, 20. yüzyılda tanıtılan diğer ulusal bayraklarda da kullanılmıştır, bunlar arasında Kazakistan (1917), Azerbaycan (1918, 1991'de yeniden tanıtıldı), Rif Cumhuriyeti (1921), Pakistan (1947), Malezya (1948), Moritanya (1959), Keşmir (1974), Sahra Arap Demokratik Cumhuriyeti (1976) ve Kuzey Kıbrıs (1983'den itibaren) gibi devletlerin bayrakları bulunmaktadır.Birkaç yıldızın yanında hilal bulunan ulusal bayraklar:Yıldız, hilal ve diğer sembolleri taşıyan ulusal bayraklar ve armalar:

=== İNCELENEN KAYIT ===
Politika:

states.db9355b6a149:
SUMMARY OF FINAL DECISION (ARTICLE 60 GDPR)
Published in the register of final decisions; national reference LSA-2025-0117

Parties
Controller: Murmur International Unlimited Company ('MIUC'), the EU establishment of the Murmur social app. MIUC determines the purposes and means of processing of the personal data of users in the EU/EEA.
Processor: Murmur, Inc. ('MINC'), established in the United States, which operates the app's infrastructure, engineering and security functions on MIUC's behalf under a data processing agreement.
Other actor: BountyHarbor B.V. ('BountyHarbor'), a contractor engaged by MINC to run the public bug bounty programme and to triage incoming reports.

Lead supervisory authority and procedure
1. The national data protection authority of Member State A (the 'LSA') acts as lead supervisory authority under Article 56(1) GDPR because MIUC is the controller's main establishment in the Union and takes the decisions on the processing of EU/EEA users' data. Supervisory authorities in all other Member States where the app is used were concerned supervisory authorities ('CSAs').
2. The LSA opened an inquiry on 4 February 2025 after receiving MIUC's breach notification. The inquiry examined compliance with Article 33(1) and Article 33(5) GDPR. An application by MIUC to extend the deadline for its submissions on the preliminary draft was granted for two weeks; a request for an oral hearing was refused because the facts were not in dispute. The LSA sent two requests for information, on 3 March and 9 April 2025, and both were answered within the deadlines set. The inquiry did not examine the security of processing under Article 32; account-recovery security is the subject of a separate inquiry opened in 2024.
3. The LSA circulated its draft decision to the CSAs on 21 May 2025 under Article 60(3), proposing an administrative fine in the range of EUR 130,000 to EUR 260,000. Three CSAs raised objections. Two argued that the proposed fine was too low to be dissuasive; a third argued that MIUC had also infringed Article 34 by not informing affected users. The LSA did not follow the objections, and the matter was referred to the European Data Protection Board under Article 65(1)(a).
4. In its binding decision of 30 September 2025, the Board found the objection concerning Article 34 not to be 'relevant and reasoned' within the meaning of Article 4(24), and therefore did not rule on it. It found the objections on the fine relevant and reasoned and instructed the LSA to reassess the amount so that it is effective, proportionate and dissuasive.

Facts
5. Version 9.14 of the Android app, released on 5 November 2023, contained a defect: when a user with the 'protected posts' setting switched on changed the e-mail address linked to the account, the setting was silently switched off and the user's posts became publicly visible. The defect affected 61,940 users in the EU/EEA until a fix was deployed on 11 January 2025. The iOS and web versions were not affected. The defect originated in a change to the account-settings service, which re-created a user's privacy preferences with default values whenever the linked e-mail address was updated. Users were shown no message; the setting appeared as switched off only if they reopened the privacy menu.
6. On Friday 27 December 2024 an external researcher submitted a report describing the defect through the bug bounty programme. The report was received by BountyHarbor, whose triage analyst validated it and forwarded it to MINC's product security team on Sunday 29 December 2024.
7. MINC's product security team reproduced the defect on 2 January 2025 and escalated it to MINC's legal team, which concluded on Friday 3 January 2025 that the defect amounted to a personal data breach. Under MINC's internal incident-response plan, the person responsible for informing MIUC's Data Protection Officer was on holiday leave until 6 January; the plan named no deputy. MINC's legal team informed MIUC's DPO office on Tuesday 7 January 2025.
8. MIUC notified the LSA through its online breach notification form on Wednesday 8 January 2025. MIUC's internal breach register entry for the incident, produced during the inquiry, recorded the defect and the fix date but did not record the number of affected users, the reasons for the delay in notification, or the effects of the breach on the users concerned.

Submissions of MIUC
9. MIUC submitted that it became aware of the breach only on 7 January 2025, when its DPO office was informed, and that its notification on 8 January was therefore made well within 72 hours. It further submitted that the holiday period and the conduct of a contractor engaged by its processor were outside its control, and that it had cooperated fully with the inquiry.
10. MIUC also pointed to the swift remediation of the defect, the absence of any complaint from affected users, and a revised incident-response plan, adopted on 14 March 2025, which requires its processor to notify MIUC within 24 hours of any suspected personal data breach and names three deputies for every role.

Assessment of the LSA
11. Article 33(1) requires the controller to notify a personal data breach 'without undue delay and, where feasible, not later than 72 hours after having become aware of it'. Article 33(2) requires the processor to notify the controller without undue delay after becoming aware of a breach.
12. The LSA does not accept that awareness can be postponed by the internal arrangements of the controller's processor. A controller that relies on a processor must ensure that the arrangements it puts in place allow it to become aware of breaches promptly. Taking into account that MINC's legal team had concluded on 3 January 2025 that a personal data breach had occurred, the LSA finds that MIUC should have become aware of the breach by 3 January 2025 at the latest. The 72-hour period therefore expired on 6 January 2025, and the notification of 8 January 2025 was late. MIUC infringed Article 33(1).
13. The breach register entry did not contain the facts relating to the breach, its effects and the remedial action taken in a form that enabled the LSA to verify compliance. MIUC infringed Article 33(5).
14. MINC is not established in the Union and is not an addressee of this decision. The LSA makes no finding against MINC or BountyHarbor; their conduct is relevant only insofar as MIUC is responsible for the arrangements it has made with its processor.

Corrective measures and fine
15. In assessing the fine under Article 83(2), the LSA took into account that the infringement of Article 33(1) concerned a delay of a few days but revealed a systemic weakness in the controller's arrangements; that the infringements were negligent, not intentional; that the underlying defect was corrected within days of being reported; and that MIUC is part of a large undertaking with worldwide annual turnover of approximately USD 3.4 billion. The LSA also took into account that MIUC had no previous infringements of Article 33, that it cooperated with the inquiry, and that the affected data were posts that users had chosen to restrict to approved followers, some of which may reveal sensitive information about the users. Infringements of Article 33 are subject to the maximum in Article 83(4).
16. Following the Board's binding decision, the LSA imposed on MIUC an administrative fine of EUR 425,000 and issued a reprimand under Article 58(2)(b).
17. The final decision was adopted on 18 November 2025 and notified to MIUC the same day. MIUC may appeal to the competent national court within 28 days of notification. A translation of this summary into the languages of the CSAs will follow.

Other matters
18. During the inquiry the LSA received a complaint from a user in Member State C about the suspension of her account in February 2025. That complaint concerns a different matter and is handled in a separate procedure.
19. MIUC asked that its worldwide turnover be redacted in the published version of the decision. The LSA agreed to publish an approximate figure only.
20. The LSA reviewed the revised incident-response plan of 14 March 2025 during the inquiry. Without prejudice to future supervision, the plan appears to address the weaknesses identified in paragraph 12, in particular the absence of deputies and of a fixed deadline for the processor to inform the controller.
